thread:
maria_oncall: urgent — multiple customers reporting 503s + timeouts on hosted API /v1/generate starting ~2026-03-17T12:34:xxZ after a canary flip. error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~18% for the past 10m. customers complaining about retries and billing noise.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: release/2026.03.17-canary-config-v2 — feature 'unscoped_config' enabled on 10% canary at 12:33:47 UTC.

sam_platform: copying logs now. can anyone confirm which config key was toggled? was this the flag from the recent rollout doc?

lee_sre: I’m seeing gateway logs showing upstream 503s with auth negotiation failures, not typical model OOMs. snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T12:34:10Z] gateway: upstream=upstream-gen-3 response=503 reason="auth_negotiation_failed" tenant=unknown route=/v1/generate trace=abc123
[2026-03-17T12:34:11Z] auth-proxy: token-rewrite: found header X-Api-Key but scope=null -> rejected
```

jen_support: impacted customers: acct-847 (high qps), acct-190 (billing alerts). they report timeouts then retries. please prioritize rollback if this was introduced by the flag.

maria_oncall: agreed. sam do we have permission to rollback the flag across canary? need coordination with platform so we don't flip unrelated regions.

sam_platform: starting rollback for 'unscoped_config' on canary now — pushing false to 10% slice. will tag and notify. ETA ~2m.

deploy-bot: rollback executed by sam_platform at 12:36:05 UTC — flag 'unscoped_config' -> false for canary slice.

observability-bot: metric update: within 90s of rollback error-rate on /v1/generate falling from 18% -> 0.9% across canary. latency P95 normalizing.

lee_sre: errors dropped but seeing a set of residual 503s for requests that used legacy API keys (tenant header missing). looks like the flag briefly removed tenant-scoping logic and gateway forwarded requests without tenant context -> upstream rejects. will run targeted healing for token mapping.

jen_support: I’ll message the top 3 affected customers with a status update and apology. can we provide repro steps so they can validate?

lee_sre: repro steps for internal triage and customer validation:
1) curl reproduce (shows 503 when flag active):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwoood-inference.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Api-Key: <legacy-key>" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
expected: 200, actual (during fault): 503 + body {"error":"auth_negotiation_failed"}.
2) check gateway logs for trace-id header X-Trace-Id returned in 503 response; grep for "auth_negotiation_failed".
3) for engineers: enable debug auth-proxy on a staging instance and toggle 'unscoped_config' locally to reproduce routing change.
```yaml
# quick config snippet
feature_flags:
  unscoped_config: true # causes tenant header stripping in this faulty build
```

maria_oncall: next steps:
- sam_platform: confirm rollback persisted to all canary nodes and no gradual re-enable job exists.
- lee_sre: collect a compact list of 5 trace ids and attach to support ticket.
- jen_support: update customers with ETA for full root-cause and any billing remediation.

sam_platform: rollback persisted and verified across canary, no automated re-enable. I also disabled the CI gate that would auto-promote this flag.

lee_sre: attaching first batch of traces: trace ids abc123, def456, ghi789, jkl012, mno345. forwarding to support.

jen_support: sent update to customers; they confirmed reduced errors on their side. one customer asked if the extra retries will be refunded — can finance advise? tagging later.

maria_oncall: quick RCA draft: mis-scoped flag "unscoped_config" removed tenant-scoping guard for a short window during canary. gateway forwarded requests with null tenant causing upstream auth-proxy to reject -> 503s. mitigation: immediate rollback, disable auto-promote, add stricter canary guard and synthetic tests that exercise legacy keys.

sam_platform: creating follow-up tickets: 1) add unit/integration test to auth-proxy for tenant-less requests, 2) add rollout-safety check to flag service, 3) run retrospective with platform and devex.

lee_sre: postmortem will include timeline + customer impact + remediation items. I'll drop traces and logs into the incident doc.

jen_support: closing loop with customers now. thanks team. :heart:

maria_oncall: incident resolving — moving to postmortem. if anything else flares up reopen. :white_check_mark:
